full_judgment: 2. Facts, leading to filing of this civil appeal, in short, are that the appellant filed an application under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949 for the purpose of pre-emption of the homestead land described in the schedule of the petition stating, inter alia, that one Entaj Ali Mondal, Hasen Ali Mondal, Zabbar Mondal and Kobat Ali were the original owners of the suit land. The SA and RS records were correctly published in their names and they made a family arrangement by which Zabbar Mondal got 20 decimals of land from the case plot. Zabbar Mondal died leaving behind three sons namely Zulhaq, Golam Mondal and Haider Mondal and three daughters namely, Amena, Komela and Joynab. They were in possession of the case land as homestead, thus the opposite party No. 2-Golam Mondal secretly sold the scheduled land of the alleged Deed No. 2869 of 2002 dated 2-4-2002 by the registered deed. The scheduled 10 decimals homestead land were transferred with 4 decimals of land of Dariapur Mouza appertaining to Khatian No. 1931 and SA Plot No. 106. The opposite party No. 2 did not possess the alleged 04 decimals of land. Though it has been shown to be an exchange deed but actually the alleged deed is nothing but out and out a sale deed. The value of the scheduled land is more than the exchanged land. The opposite parties have just created a colourable deed to defeat the rights of preemption. The opposite party No. 2, Md Golam Mondal sold the land to the opposite party No. 1 secretly and beyond the knowledge of the petitioner. The opposite party No. 1 is a stranger in the case jote. The petitioner first came to know about the sale on 10-1-2002. He deposited the consideration money together with compensation. Hence, demanded the case land by filing the Preemption Miscellaneous Case.
